version.changelog: Declared as the base skill the 12306/pdd/hospital skills depend on. Ships requirements-adb.txt (pinned OCR-loop venv deps) so dependents install from $BASE/requirements-adb.txt. Every ocr_bridge.py invocation is documented as $PY $BASE/... so commands work from any working directory; OCR_BRIDGE_DIR no longer doubles as the module location.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed Android phone automation bridge, but it needs review because it exposes direct tap and typing controls on a connected phone without enforcing its own confirmation rule for sensitive actions.

dimensions.detail: ADB screenshots, accessibility-tree reads, clipboard use, localhost Appium, and private cache directories are coherent for Android automation and are disclosed, but they may expose sensitive on-device content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a local venv with pinned Python dependencies and local scripts; I found no remote payload retrieval beyond normal package installation. The start script uses fixed cache paths under the user's home directory and assumes the default OpenClaw skill path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation tells agents to confirm irreversible actions, but the executable entry points perform tap, coordinate tap, OCR tap, accessibility tap, and typing commands immediately when invoked. There is no dry-run gate, confirmation token, or enforced distinction between inspection and state-changing commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: One-shot Appium commands are documented to stop services they start, while persistent daemon mode is opt-in through start_bridge.sh. The daemon and Appium are background processes with private IPC and loopback binding, but users must stop them when finished.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifacts: OCR, accessibility, ADB, uiautomator2, and Appium are used to read and control Android apps. The concern is proportionality: the skill can tap, scroll, type, read screenshots/accessibility trees, and affect bookings, purchases, or payment screens on any connected device.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to control a USB-connected Android phone. Keep Appium bound to 127.0.0.1, use one-shot commands when possible, stop the daemon after use, and require explicit human confirmation before any booking, checkout, order submission, payment-adjacent tap, or typed sensitive information.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material review concern: the documented confirmation boundary for irreversible device actions is not enforced by the tap/type-capable scripts.
[LP3] unexpected: Partially accepted: broad phone-control authority is purpose-aligned, but the skill does not provide an enforceable permission boundary between read-only inspection and state-changing actions.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the Appium fallback is clearly documented in SKILL.md, and the package also includes the OCR primary path, so this is not a deceptive purpose mismatch.
[E2] expected: Downgraded: the code passes the current environment to the Appium subprocess while setting Android SDK variables; I found no evidence of credential collection, logging, or exfiltration.
[TM1] expected: Downgraded: the rm -f commands remove fixed bridge IPC/cache files, not broad or user-supplied paths.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: background Appium/daemon use is explicitly documented as opt-in persistent mode, not an automatic startup hook or cross-session backdoor.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partially accepted: the broader action surface is mostly disclosed, but the daemon exposes high-impact tap/type/JS-style controls without an enforced consent mechanism.
[TM3] expected: Downgraded: the cited world-writable text appears in a safety check that rejects group/world-writable IPC files.
[AST4] expected: Downgraded: subprocess use is expected for ADB/Appium automation and uses argument lists rather than shell command strings in the inspected paths.
[TT2] expected: Downgraded: ANDROID_HOME/ANDROID_SDK_ROOT are expected inputs for starting Appium; no command injection or network transmission was evident.
[AST3] expected: Downgraded: dynamic __import__('re') loads the standard regex module for parsing bounds and is not an arbitrary plugin loader.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: mixed Appium and direct uiautomator2 behavior is awkwardly documented but disclosed across the skill as primary OCR plus Appium fallback.
